checks.statement: the two a=0 columns have private Hall rows 1 and 2
checks.detail: a=0 source has only c_g, hence only its two terminal path rows

checks.statement: the a=2 pair is triangular on rows -g-2 and -g
checks.detail: the plus support begins at -g, while the minus support begins at -g-2

checks.statement: the q=2 base determinant is an explicit endpoint product
the q=2 initialization block has full rank for every g>=2
checks.detail: all rising factorials and g-1,g+1,g+3 are nonzero

checks.statement: the symbolic product equals every generated q=2 base determinant

verdict: The q=2 initialization block in source Hall coordinates consists of two private a=0 endpoints and a triangular a=2 pair. Its determinant is -3(g-1)(g+1)(g+3)(4 rising g)^2(2 rising g)^2, nonzero for every g>=2. Thus no q=2 kernel class can be born at initialization; later extensions are covered by the even boundary and stable transport laws.
